assumptions: Licensed partners execute regulated legal and collection actions.
Success fees are deducted only after cleared funds under a compliant payment structure.
The initial portfolio excludes disputed and clearly unrecoverable claims.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A controlled portfolio showing recovery rates and time by claim segment, positive contribution after partner share and support, creditor acceptance of fees, low dispute and complaint rates, repeat accountant referrals, and a reviewed legal and payment structure.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Charging on cleared cash aligns value with a painful outcome and data-driven routing may preserve debtor relationships better than default escalation.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Late payment creates direct liquidity and recovery costs, and a success fee lowers purchase friction, though willingness to share the proposed percentage remains untested.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: No-recovery-no-fee pricing is attractive to creditors but invites adverse selection, delayed cash conversion, partner sharing, disputes, compliance overhead, and uncertain recovery-adjusted margins.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish micro and small B2B creditors reached through accountants form a large, coherent beachhead, although claim quality and average recoverable value matter more than headline invoice volume.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Neutral routing could establish a differentiated aggregator position, but collection agencies, legal firms, and invoice platforms already own capabilities and relationships.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful routing can extend into monitoring, credit scoring, reminders, mediation, legal recovery, insurance, and working-capital products.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Recovery outcomes can improve route selection and accountant distribution can compound, but mandates are nonexclusive and capable incumbents can accumulate similar data.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Outcome pricing and least-destructive route selection offer a meaningful convenience and risk advantage over choosing a collection provider directly.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Late-payment pressure is persistent and digitized bookkeeping aids intake, but the supplied evidence does not identify a uniquely temporary opening.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accountants are a logical repeatable referral channel, but no agreement or invoice access exists and advisers may avoid reputational exposure.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A partner-led test fits available capital, yet legal boundaries, debtor disputes, payment handling, adverse selection, brand risk, and partner quality create substantial operational complexity.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure an exclusive or preferred accountant-platform intake channel with standardized claim data and pre-screening that rejects disputed or low-probability invoices before costly recovery work.
main_structural_strength: The revenue event is directly tied to recovered customer cash, producing strong value alignment and measurable routing outcomes.
primary_score_limiter: Adverse-selection-adjusted recovery economics and compliant execution are unknown, while access to both claims and capable partners is unsigned.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Many SMEs avoid aggressive recovery to protect customer relationships, and regulated legal or payment activity requires qualified partners.
